mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a correct definition of a physical quantity?

options.A: A physical quantity is a property of a system that can be measured and expressed as a numerical value with a unit.
options.B: A physical quantity is any concept that can be described qualitatively without measurement.
options.C: A physical quantity requires both magnitude and unit for its expression.
options.D: Physical quantities include length, mass, time, etc.

mcqs.answer: A physical quantity is any concept that can be described qualitatively without measurement.
mcqs.explanation: Option B is incorrect because a physical quantity must be measurable and expressed with a numerical value and a unit. Options A, C and D correctly describe that a physical quantity is measurable, needs a magnitude and unit, and includes examples like length, mass and time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a derived quantity that is obtained by combining fundamental quantities?
mcqs.explanation: Velocity is derived because it is defined as displacement (length) divided by time, both of which are fundamental quantities. Mass, length and time themselves are fundamental base quantities in the SI system, so they are not derived.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the SI system with the CGS system?

options.A: In SI, the unit of force is the newton, which is defined as kg·m/s², whereas in CGS the unit of force is the dyne, defined as g·cm/s².
options.B: In SI, the unit of energy is the joule, defined as kg·m²/s, whereas in CGS the unit of energy is the erg, defined as g·cm²/s².
options.C: In SI, the unit of pressure is the pascal, defined as N/m², whereas in CGS the unit of pressure is the bar, defined as 10⁵ N/m².
options.D: In SI, the unit of electric charge is the coulomb, defined as A·s, whereas in CGS the unit of electric charge is the ampere, defined as A.

mcqs.answer: In SI, the unit of force is the newton, which is defined as kg·m/s², whereas in CGS the unit of force is the dyne, defined as g·cm/s².
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly states the SI unit of force (newton) and its definition, and the CGS unit of force (dyne) with its definition. Option B is wrong because the joule is kg·m²/s², not kg·m²/s. Option C is wrong because the CGS unit of pressure is the barye, not the bar. Option D is wrong because the CGS unit of charge is the statcoulomb, not the ampere.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches each physical quantity with its SI base unit?

options.A: Length – metre (m), Mass – kilogram (kg), Time – second (s), Electric current – ampere (A)
options.B: Length – metre (m), Mass – gram (g), Time – minute (min), Electric current – coulomb (C)
options.C: Length – foot (ft), Mass – kilogram (kg), Time – second (s), Electric current – ampere (A)
options.D: Length – metre (m), Mass – kilogram (kg), Time – hour (h), Electric current – ampere (A)

mcqs.answer: Length – metre (m), Mass – kilogram (kg), Time – second (s), Electric current – ampere (A)
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the correct SI base units: metre for length, kilogram for mass, second for time, and ampere for electric current. Options B, C and D contain incorrect units (gram instead of kilogram, minute or hour instead of second, foot instead of metre, coulomb is a derived unit, not a base unit).
